title: subject_srv.exe (F-Response Subject agent) running at memory acquisition
observation: Volatility3 windows.pslist (invocation mem-dc4e0201) shows PID 1096, PPID 740 (services.exe), ImageFileName 'subject_srv.ex' (14-char kernel truncation), Wow64=True, CreateTime 2018-09-06 18:28:30 UTC, no ExitTime. Volatility3 windows.cmdline (invocation mem-e8975db8) shows the full command line: C:\windows\subject_srv.exe -s "base-hunt.shieldbase.lan:5682" -l 3262 -v "F-Response Subject" -k "155522845". Path C:\windows\ (not C:\Windows\System32) is anomalous for a legitimate Windows binary.
interpretation: Direct memory artifacts (pslist + cmdline) confirm subject_srv.exe was actively running at the moment of memory capture, listening on TCP 3262 and configured to call back to base-hunt.shieldbase.lan:5682 with an F-Response Subject identity/key. correlate_evidence('subject_srv.exe', '/root/cases/SRL-2018-RD01/analysis') was called (invocation correlation_3ec5367ec9c1) but returned verdict=ERROR because the prefetch source failed (pyscca/libscca not installed) — not because the process is absent. Per CLAUDE.md confidence-mapping rules, CONFIRMED may only be asserted when correlate_evidence returns CONFIRMED_RUNNING/CONFIRMED_HISTORICAL/MEMORY_ONLY; ERROR is not in that table, so this is labeled INFERRED with the gap documented (same pyscca blocker previously seen on SRL-2018-WKSTN and SRL-2018-DC).

title: subject_srv.exe listening on TCP 3262 with active inbound session from 172.16.5.50
observation: Volatility3 windows.netscan (invocation mem-3fb6abd0) shows: TCPv4 0.0.0.0:3262 LISTENING, PID 1096, Owner subject_srv.ex, Created 2018-09-06 18:28:32 UTC (also TCPv6 ::,3262 LISTENING same PID/time). A separate entry shows TCPv4 172.16.6.11:3262 ESTABLISHED with ForeignAddr 172.16.5.50:39372 (PID not resolved by netscan).
interpretation: CONFIRMED direct artifact: subject_srv.exe (PID 1096) is the listener on port 3262 and an active session from 172.16.5.50 was connected to that port at capture time. 172.16.5.50 was also seen connecting to subject_srv.exe on SRL-2018-WKSTN (port 3262) in a prior session, suggesting 172.16.5.50 is a consistent operator/controller host reaching F-Response agents across multiple hosts on this network.

title: p.exe (c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe) — long-lived process repeatedly spawning rundll32.exe over multiple days
observation: Volatility3 windows.pslist (mem-dc4e0201) shows PID 8260 ImageFileName 'p.exe', PPID 5948 (cmd.exe), CreateTime 2018-08-30 22:15:18 UTC, ExitTime N/A (still running at capture ~2018-09-06). windows.cmdline (mem-e8975db8) shows PID 5948 Args 'C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /C c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe' and PID 8260 Args 'c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe'. pslist further shows three rundll32.exe children of PID 8260 with empty Args, all with short lifetimes: PID 5768 (CreateTime 2018-09-05 12:01:32, ExitTime 2018-09-05 12:01:40), PID 1424 (CreateTime 2018-09-06 14:58:41, ExitTime 2018-09-06 14:58:45), PID 7552 (CreateTime 2018-09-06 17:26:32, ExitTime 2018-09-06 17:26:35).
interpretation: p.exe runs from C:\windows\temp\perfmon\ — a non-standard staging path masquerading as a performance-monitor utility — and has persisted in memory for over 6 days (2018-08-30 22:15:18 through at least 2018-09-06 17:26:35), periodically spawning short-lived rundll32.exe instances with no visible command-line arguments. This pattern (long-lived parent in a Temp directory repeatedly launching rundll32.exe with empty args, days apart) is consistent with a beacon/loader using rundll32.exe (LOLBAS) for periodic payload execution. INFERRED — no Amcache/Prefetch/MFT corroboration available (MEMORY_ONLY host); execution path and timing pattern are the supporting artifacts.

title: PowerShell remoting session (no-profile, stdin mode) spawned via WmiPrvSE, repeatedly invoking rundll32.exe
observation: windows.pslist (mem-dc4e0201) shows PID 2876 WmiPrvSE.exe (PPID 868, svchost DcomLaunch) spawned PID 8712 powershell.exe at 2018-08-30 16:43:36 UTC, which spawned PID 5848 powershell.exe at 16:43:42 UTC. windows.cmdline (mem-e8975db8) shows PID 5848 Args: "c:\\windows\\syswow64\\windowspowershell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe" -Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile. pslist shows PID 5848 (PPID for several rundll32.exe with empty Args) spawned rundll32.exe children at 2018-08-30 18:31:04 (PID 6768), 21:40:18 (PID 5452), 21:40:42 (PID 5588), 22:31:57 (PID 2216), 22:45:25 (PID 4108), and 2018-08-31 00:56:14 (PID 8148) — all short-lived (seconds).
interpretation: A PowerShell process launched via WMI (WmiPrvSE.exe) with -s -NoLogo -NoProfile (consistent with a remote/headless PowerShell session, e.g. PSRemoting/WinRM, which windows.netscan shows listening on TCP 5985/47001 on this host) repeatedly invoked rundll32.exe with no arguments over several hours on 2018-08-30. This is INFERRED lateral-movement/execution activity: an attacker likely established a remote PowerShell session and used rundll32.exe (LOLBAS) for repeated payload execution, the same technique later continued by p.exe (see related finding). No Amcache/Prefetch/MFT corroboration available (MEMORY_ONLY host).

title: Repeated outbound connections from 172.16.6.11 to 172.16.4.10:8080 (beacon-like pattern)
observation: windows.netscan (mem-3fb6abd0) shows at least 10 TCPv4 connection records with LocalAddr 172.16.6.11 and ForeignAddr 172.16.4.10, ForeignPort 8080, across states CLOSE_WAIT (6 entries: local ports 52703, 50253, 50263, 50259, 49774, 50257, 50254, 50258), ESTABLISHED (2 entries: local ports 49787, 49786), and CLOSED (2 entries: local ports 63931, 49790, 49735). PID/Owner could not be resolved by netscan for these (listed as '-').
interpretation: A high volume of repeated connections from this host to a single internal IP:port (172.16.4.10:8080) — many left in CLOSE_WAIT — is anomalous and was previously flagged on SRL-2018-WKSTN as an unattributed pattern not on the prd.json IOC list (172.16.4.10 is not in known_iocs/suspicious_patterns). Pattern is consistent with C2 beaconing or a proxy/relay, but cannot be attributed to a specific process because netscan did not resolve a PID. HYPOTHESIS pending further corroboration (process owning these sockets could not be determined from available memory artifacts).

title: Cross-subnet connections suggest lateral movement: RDP/SMB to 172.16.4.5, WinRM to 172.16.5.21, SMB inbound from 172.16.6.14
interpretation: This host (172.16.6.11) shows repeated RDP attempts to 172.16.4.5, an active SMB session to 172.16.4.5, a WinRM (5985) connection attempt to 172.16.5.21, an inbound SMB connection from 172.16.6.14, and an LDAP query to 172.16.4.4 (likely the domain controller). Taken together this is INFERRED evidence of lateral-movement activity touching multiple hosts across 172.16.4.x and 172.16.6.x subnets, consistent with the R&D-subnet lateral-movement theme in prd.json (target 172.16.6.12 not directly observed here, but 172.16.6.14 and 172.16.4.5 are in the same address ranges). No process attribution possible — netscan did not resolve PIDs for these sockets.
